title: Committee of Supply − Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: US on China South China Sea
sections.summary: The US administration has called China's island installations illegal and may act to stop China accessing them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the South China Sea, the United States (US) administration has recently mentioned that they see China's developments of installations in the island as illegal and steps may be taken to stop China from accessing them.

sections.label: North Korea nuclear test and killing
sections.summary: North Korea held its fifth nuclear test in September 2016, and Kim Jong-Nam was killed in Kuala Lumpur, possibly by VX nerve agent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Closer to the region, along the Korean peninsula, North Korea has carried out its fifth nuclear test in September 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even closer to home, in the Kuala Lumpur airport, a North Korean national, Kim Jong-Nam, a half-brother of North Korea's leader, was killed under mysterious circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It appears that nerve agent VX, classified as a "weapon of mass destruction", might have been used in the process.

sections.label: MINDEF cyber systems attack
sections.summary: MINDEF reported in recent days that its cyber systems were attacked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just the last few days, the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) reported that there was an attack on its cyber systems.

sections.label: US Strategic Framework Agreement
sections.summary: The Strategic Framework Agreement with the US formalised Singapore's bilateral security and defence relationship with the US.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Our Strategic Framework Agreement with the US formalised our bilateral security and defence relationship.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia Defence Cooperation Agreement
sections.summary: 2017 marks the 10th anniversary of the unimplemented DCA, and the question asks the Ministry's view on fresh discussions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, 2017 marks the 10th anniversary of the yet to be implemented Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) between Singapore and Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2007, Indonesia sought to review DCA after agreeing details with Singapore, while Singapore insisted that negotiations were complete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In April last year, however, Jakarta confirmed that it was intensifying cooperation in law enforcement in lieu of an extradition treaty and was reported to have given Singapore a list of fugitives, for follow-up and assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In light of the 50th Anniversary of Singapore-Indonesia diplomatic ties and the signing of the Eastern Boundary Treaty, what is the Ministry's perspective of initiating fresh discussions on DCA in the name of renewed military cooperation and stronger diplomatic links between both countries?

sections.label: Singapore targeted by militants
sections.summary: Singapore was targeted by Jemaah Islamiyah after 9/11 and in August last year by a militant group planning a rocket attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Closer to home, Singapore itself has been targeted by the Jemaah Islamiyah (JI) in the aftermath of 9/11, and also in August last year by a militant group planning to launch a rocket at Singapore's Marina Bay.

sections.label: King's College threat breakdown
sections.summary: King's College London breaks down these threats into espionage, subversion, sabotage, cybercrime and cyber war, which is less common.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: The work from King's College London breaks down these threats into: (a) espionage, (b) subversion, (c) sabotage, (d) cybercrime and, finally, (e) cyber war, which is less common.

sections.label: Defence Technology Community growth
sections.summary: The Defence Technology Community, started in 1966, comprises DSTA, DSO, MINDEF's Future Systems and Technology Directorate, and Defence Industry and Systems Office, and has grown to 5,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Defence Technology Community (DTC), which started in 1966, comprising the Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) and DSO National Laboratories (DSO), as well as MINDEF's Future Systems and Technology Directorate, and Defence Industry and Systems Office, has grown to a 5,000-strong community today.

sections.label: ISIS unmanned aircraft unit
sections.summary: The Washington Post reported that ISIS had established a new unmanned aircraft unit of modified drones equipped with bombs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last month, the Washington Post reported that the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS) had established a new unmanned aircraft unit, comprising of fleets of modified drones equipped with bombs.

sections.label: Drone access controls and infrastructure
sections.summary: It asks whether controls and infrastructure are in place to regulate the access of drones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Do we have the controls and infrastructure in place to regulate the access of drones?

sections.label: People for homegrown weapons technology
sections.summary: It asks whether enough people can be found to develop these weapons and homegrown technologies, needing STEM backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: One of the important things, of course, is whether we can get enough people to develop these weapons, these homegrown technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: We need people with science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) backgrounds or fields.

sections.label: Third Generation SAF creation
sections.summary: In 2004, the Third Generation (3G) SAF was created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: In 2004, we created the Third Generation (3G) SAF.

sections.label: Shrinking SAF manpower
sections.summary: SAF's available Singaporean manpower will soon shrink because the total fertility rate has been low for many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Even as the threats have broadened, the Singaporean manpower that SAF can draw upon will soon shrink as our total fertility rate has been low for many years.

sections.label: Asia defence spending increase
sections.summary: Asia has outspent Europe on defence since 2012, with a 5.4% rise in military expenditure in Asia and Oceania from 2014 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Asia has spent more on its defence than Europe in absolute dollars since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In fact, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, from 2014 to 2015 alone, there was a 5.4% increase in military expenditure in Asia and Oceania, which far surpasses the 1% increase in defence spending globally.

sections.label: MINDEF servers hacked
sections.summary: The hacking of MINDEF's own servers days ago shows the threat is real and imminent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The fact that MINDEF's own servers were hacked just a few days ago highlights how real and imminent this threat is.

sections.label: NSmen trained in conventional tactics
sections.summary: Many male Singaporeans who served NS were trained in conventional tactics like jungle warfare, which may not suit today's hybrid warfare threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Many male Singaporeans who have served NS understand the importance of defending Singapore and have developed the resolve to protect our land.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: However, most of them were trained in conventional tactics, such as jungle warfare, which may not be relevant in today's hybrid warfare threats.

sections.label: NSF vocational preference initiative
sections.summary: Following CSNS recommendations and IPS survey findings, MINDEF let the first cohort of pre-enlistees indicate vocational preferences at CMPB in November last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: The CSNS Report cited a survey done by the Institute of Policy Studies where 97% of respondents felt that more could be done to match Servicemen's personal skills and abilities with NS vocations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Report also noted that CSNS had studied the Finnish and Swiss NS systems, both of which enjoy strong public support, and noted that both the Finns and the Swiss had some form of policy where conscripts could indicate their vocational preferences when enlisted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Based on these findings, one of the CSNS recommendations was to consider the vocational interests of NSFs when assigning them to vocations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In line with CSNS' recommendations, MINDEF allowed the first cohort of pre-enlistees under the new initiative to indicate vocational preferences when they reported to the Central Manpower Base in November last year.

sections.label: Next Generation SAF transformation
sections.summary: SAF must transform to the Next Generation SAF, as it did for 3G, while thanking over one million NSmen for their duty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We have talked about the 3G transformation for a number of years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And like Members here, we recognise that this year is a very special year ‒ 75 years since the fall of Singapore, 50 years since NS' inception.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Together with all Members here, we want to thank the more than one million committed NSmen who have done their duty faithfully and built a strong SAF to protect Singapore and Singaporeans these past decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As we did for the 3G SAF transformation efforts, SAF must once again transform to the Next Generation SAF, to be better positioned for the future.

sections.label: China India ASEAN economic growth
sections.summary: China grew 10% yearly for 30 years, India about 6%, and ASEAN averaged 6%, above the global 4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: China's economy grew for 30 years phenomenally at an average of 10% every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: India's economy also grew, albeit at a slower rate of about 6% per annum over a similar period from 1979 for 30 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This massive growth lifted all boats in the global economy, particularly for Asia, including ASEAN, which grew an average of 6% per annum, well above the global average of 4%.

sections.label: Enhanced DCA and Australia partnership
sections.summary: Singapore signed an enhanced DCA with the US in 2015 and a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Australia last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For other initiatives, we will lean forward if other countries want us to participate further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We signed an enhanced DCA with the US in 2015 and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Australia last year.

sections.label: Russia Cyber Army spending
sections.summary: Russia spends $300 million annually on its roughly 1,000-person Cyber Army, according to Kommersant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Russia spends $300 million annually on its "Cyber Army" of about 1,000 people, according to the Kommersant, their local newspaper.

sections.label: Ukraine and Estonia cyberattacks
sections.summary: Ukraine's grid suffered cyberattacks, including one in December 2015, and Estonia plans a digital copy of the nation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Ukraine's power grid has been hit by several cyberattacks, and one such attack in December 2015 cut off power to an area about 20 times the size of Singapore, and this was in the middle of winter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Their people and government understand this threat particularly well, because they have been a target of well-orchestrated cyberattacks since 2007 for the last decade, so much so that Estonia plans to make a digital copy of the entire nation, everything from birth records, property deeds, bank data, all government records.

sections.label: MINDEF I-net breach disclosure
sections.summary: The speech was prepared for weeks, but MINDEF recently disclosed a breach in its I-net system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As it happens, we have prepared this speech for some weeks now, but MINDEF recently disclosed a breach in its I-net system.

sections.label: New Defence Cyber Organisation
sections.summary: MINDEF and SAF will stand up a new cyber command called the Defence Cyber Organisation at the highest organisational level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In a clear and unmitigated recognition that the cyber domain is the battlefield today, MINDEF and SAF will stand up a new cyber command.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It will be called the Defence Cyber Organisation (DCO) and placed at the highest level of our organisational hierarchy.

sections.label: DCO steady state size
sections.summary: In the steady state, DCO will have about 2,600 soldiers supported by DSTA and DSO scientists and engineers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the steady state, DCO will have about 2,600 soldiers, supported by scientists and engineers in DSTA and DSO.

sections.label: Defence engineers and scientists community
sections.summary: There is a 5,000-strong growing community of defence engineers and scientists, and such scholarships and awards will increase by 40% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We now have a 5,000-strong and growing community of defence engineers and scientists.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We will increase such scholarships and awards by 40% by 2025.

sections.label: DSTA lab AI seed grant
sections.summary: DSTA's new lab will exploit AI and data analytics, and two new labs will get a $45 million annual seed grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: DSTA's new lab will exploit AI and data analytics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We will give these two new labs a seed grant of $45 million annually as a start, so that they can lead in more experimentation and innovation.

sections.label: Cyber command and conventional training
sections.summary: Even as a new cyber command, technology labs and the inaugural Singapore Defence Technology Summit are set up, conventional force and terrorism training must not be neglected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Even as we set up a new cyber command and technology labs, even as we want to host the inaugural Singapore Defence Technology Summit, I agree completely with Member Teo Ho Pin that we must never neglect to train the SAF's conventional force against traditional threats and, as Mr Cedric Foo pointed out, terrorism.

sections.label: Training camps and overseas grounds
sections.summary: A minimum baseload of training camps is needed, existing ones will be maximised, and over-dependence on overseas training grounds must be guarded against.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We do need a minimum baseload of training camps, but we will maximise what we have.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And we must guard against over-dependence on overseas training grounds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: It is not possible for all our NSmen to only train overseas because the bulk of our training is still conducted here, especially for the Army.

sections.label: New SAFTI City construction
sections.summary: A new SAFTI City will be built for realistic training, taking a decade to complete and costing approximately $900 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For SAF to train realistically and effectively, we will build a new SAFTI City, because even peacekeeping and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) missions are likely to be conducted in built-up cities and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The new SAFTI City will take a decade to complete and cost approximately $900 million.

sections.label: SAFTI City training terrains
sections.summary: SAFTI City aims to let any battalion fight across different terrains successively, as in real life missions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The idea of what the new SAFTI City wants to accomplish is to allow any battalion to fight across different terrains successively, as they would do in real life missions.

sections.label: Sector 2 urban features
sections.summary: Sector 2 will have high-rise interconnected buildings, basement car parks, a bus interchange and an underground MRT station for counter terrorism and urban operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Sector 2 will have high-rise and interconnected buildings, basement car parks, a bus interchange and an underground Mass Rapid Transit station which will be useful for Counter Terrorism and High Intensity Urban Operations, as Members talked about.

sections.label: Defence budget growth projection
sections.summary: MINDEF projects the defence budget can stay on a 3%-4% yearly growth trajectory, at least keeping pace with inflation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Even with new demands that I have sketched out for the Next Gen SAF, MINDEF has projected that our defence budget can be maintained on the current trajectory of 3%-4% growth each year, which would allow us to at least keep pace with inflation.

sections.label: Frigate Ship Management System savings
sections.summary: The Navy's Frigate Ship Management System reduces maintenance time by 93% and saved $40 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We did it through the Republic of Singapore Navy's new Frigate Ship Management System.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This system reduces maintenance time by 93% and saved us $40 million.

sections.label: SMART magazine savings
sections.summary: The SMART magazine will save $1.4 million each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Indeed, that is what the SMART magazine does.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And it will save $1.4 million each year.

sections.label: Defence investment and political will
sections.summary: At each step Singapore needs to invest in defence and political will, and SAF stands ready as guardians of peace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Whether we were a poor country as a new nation having to spend on defence or as an up and rising country with other needs and now having to face an ageing society with an uncertain world, at each step, you need to invest in defence and you need political will.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I want to thank the strong commitment of our NSmen, the unwavering support of the Members of this House and the unshakeable resolve of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: With these elements, SAF stands ready as guardians of the peace and defenders of our way of life.

sections.label: Smoking trends among Servicemen
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to study smoking trends among Servicemen, examine impediments to reducing smoking prevalence and introduce interventions against smoking culture in bases and training areas.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the importance of NS and the costs associated with a lack of enforcement, I would like to urge the Ministry to conduct a study of smoking trends among its Servicemen, examine the impediments to achieving a greater reduction in smoking prevalence and introduce active interventions to root out any smoking culture within bases and in training areas.

sections.label: SAF training safety efforts
sections.summary: The speaker notes MINDEF's assurance on training safety, SAF's Safety core value, the SSRD and ERPSS, and asks what additional efforts make training safer and how these are communicated to families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: MINDEF has given the assurance that maintaining training safety is a key element of a strong and professional armed force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that in 2013, SAF added Safety as its eighth core value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: A Safety and Systems Review Directorate (SSRD) was formed to oversee the conduct of safety and systems reviews for MINDEF and SAF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: SSRD set up its first external review panel, the External Review Panel on SAF Safety (ERPSS) in 2013 to review various aspects of SAF safety over its three-year tenure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Can MINDEF share what additional efforts have or are being made to make training regimes safer for our NSmen and how these efforts are being communicated to their family members and loved ones to provide greater assurance?

sections.label: ACCORD proposals implementation status
sections.summary: The speaker notes that 14 of 18 ACCORD proposals were completed as of last year and asks MINDEF for a status update on the remaining proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As of last year, Senior Minister of State Dr Maliki Bin Osman updated that 14 of the 18 ACCORD proposals had been completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide a status update on the implementation of the remaining ACCORD proposals over the last year?

sections.label: Building urban and cyber defence
sections.summary: The speaker states that based on regional defence spending and new security threats, Singapore needs to build defence and fighting capabilities in urban and cyber warfare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: Based on the defence spending in our region and new threats to our security, we need to build our defence and fighting capabilities in urban and cyber warfare.

sections.label: Lack of Total Defence readiness
sections.summary: The speaker states that despite much effort, there is a general lack of understanding and Total Defence readiness among Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: Despite much effort, there is a general lack of understanding and total defence readiness among Singaporeans.

sections.label: Youths patrolling and Total Defence readiness
sections.summary: The speaker says these youths performed their patrolling duties diligently and that Singaporeans' operational readiness in Total Defence must be constantly tested.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: These youths performed their duties very diligently while ensuring safety and security in the areas patrolled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: We need to constantly test the operational readiness of Singaporeans in Total Defence.

sections.label: Soldier Strong initiative
sections.summary: The Soldier Strong initiative develops physically strong, psychologically resilient soldiers, and NSmen get enhanced fitness training at a new Centre for Excellence for Soldier Performance operational end-2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, we ensure that every soldier is individually "strong".

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is why we have launched the "Soldier Strong" initiative to develop soldiers who are physically strong, psychologically resilient and committed to the defence of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under the "Soldier Strong" programme, NSmen will have access to enhanced fitness training programmes at the new Centre for Excellence for Soldier Performance that will be operational at the end of 2017.

sections.label: Pre-enlistees indicate vocation interest
sections.summary: Since November last year, pre-enlistees have indicated interest in 33 vocations across SAF, the Singapore Police Force and the Singapore Civil Defence Force.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since November last year, pre-enlistees have indicated their interest in 33 vocations across SAF, the Singapore Police Force and the Singapore Civil Defence Force.

sections.label: Enlistees interest in Infantry Guards
sections.summary: The SAF's experience is that most enlistees want to contribute and sweat it out, and in the latest enlistment exercise 60% of pre-enlistees indicated interest in Infantry and Guards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That has actually not been the SAF's experience, which is that most enlistees today want to contribute to the best of their abilities and sweat it out if possible.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, in the latest enlistment exercise, 60% of pre-enlistees indicated interest in Infantry and Guards.

sections.label: NSF deployment from August
sections.summary: NSFs will be deployed to these vocations from August this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: NSFs will be deployed to these vocations from August this year.

sections.label: External Review Panel safety review
sections.summary: MINDEF convened an External Review Panel of safety experts in 2013, which completed a three-year review and concluded SAF's health and safety system is internationally one of the best, with areas for improvement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2013, MINDEF convened an External Review Panel, comprising prominent safety experts outside of SAF, to review safety in SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Panel has recently completed this three-year safety review and concluded that our health and safety system are internationally one of the best but, of course, there are areas for improvement.

sections.label: NS50 vouchers and memberships
sections.summary: To commemorate NS50, Minister Ng announced each NSman will receive $100 in vouchers and, for ORDN NSmen, a one-year SAFRA or HomeTeamNS membership.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To commemorate NS50, Minister Ng announced last month that each NSman will receive $100 in vouchers and, for ORDN NSmen, a one-year membership to SAFRA or HomeTeamNS.

sections.label: NS recognition campaign supporters
sections.summary: Over 250 organisations will support a month-long recognition campaign from July to early August through discounts, souvenirs, HR policies and ceremonies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More than 250 organisations will support the month-long recognition campaign from July to the first week of August, through retail discounts, free souvenirs, more NS-friendly human resource policies and rededication ceremonies.

sections.label: SkillsFuture accreditation for BMT enlistees
sections.summary: From this year, SkillsFuture Singapore will accredit enlistees with skills such as teamwork honed during BMT.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From this year, SkillsFuture Singapore will accredit enlistees with skills, such as teamwork, that are honed during BMT.

sections.label: NS as defence cornerstone
sections.summary: NS remains the cornerstone of defence and security, with trained NSmen increasing military capability and credibility against potential adversaries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: NS continues to be the cornerstone of our defence and security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our well-trained and committed NSmen increase our military capability and give us credibility when we speak.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Potential adversaries know that if they attack Singapore, it is a fight against a populace, all trained and ready to defend our sovereignty and freedom.

sections.label: Countries legislating mandatory conscription
sections.summary: Lithuania, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar have recently legislated mandatory conscription, recognising a credible military cannot be built overnight.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Others, as mentioned by Mr Baey Yam Keng – Lithuania, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar − have recently legislated mandatory conscription.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They recognise that transition from a benign to a hostile geopolitical environment can happen without warning, and a capable and credible military cannot be built overnight.

sections.label: NS role in nation-building
sections.summary: The nation-building aspect of defence will be more significant if participation is spread over all strata of society.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The nation-building aspect of defence will be more significant if its participation is spread over all strata of society." The role of NS in nation-building has become ever more salient today as we march forward in this era of globalisation.

sections.label: Incident incited Muslim-Catholic hostility
sections.summary: Activists exploited the incident to incite hostility between Muslim and predominantly European and Eurasian Catholic populations, resulting in 18 dead and 173 injured.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The activists exploited the incident to incite hostility between the Muslim and predominantly European and Eurasian Catholic populations in Singapore then.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This resulted in 18 dead, 173 injured and significant property damage.

sections.label: The Real Singapore false claim
sections.summary: The Real Singapore owners falsely claimed a Filipino family's complaints caused a scuffle at the 2015 Thaipusam procession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, the owners of the now-defunct site The Real Singapore made a false claim that a Filipino family's complaints had caused a scuffle between the Police and participants at the 2015 Thaipusam procession.

sections.label: Total Defence concept to action
sections.summary: The Government will shift Total Defence from concept to action, citing MINDEF's 2016 survey showing awareness and support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This is why the five pillars and the core message of every Singaporean standing together, playing our part to protect Singapore and our shared way of life continue to be relevant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I am glad that more than 80% of Singaporeans surveyed by MINDEF in 2016 are aware of Total Defence and more than 90% of them agree that it remains important for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The Government will, therefore, make a shift from "concept to action", and help Singaporeans understand how they can put Total Defence into action in their everyday lives.

sections.label: ISIS Southeast Asia wilayat
sections.summary: ISIS wants a wilayat in Southeast Asia and has formed Katibah Nusantara with about 1,000 Southeast Asian volunteers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ISIS wants to set up a wilayat in Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It has already formed a militant group called Katibah Nusantara comprising about 1,000 volunteers from Southeast Asia.

sections.label: Extremist groups threatening multi-religious society
sections.summary: Extremist groups spreading exclusivist and literalist Islam threaten Singapore's multi-religious society, with 31 groups backing ISIS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Around our region, the growth of extremist groups who spread exclusivist and literalist leanings in Islam poses a significant threat to our multi-religious society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We know of 31 such groups which have pledged allegiance or support for ISIS.

sections.label: Total Defence Day Ford Factory gallery
sections.summary: Last month Total Defence Day was commemorated with the revamped Japanese Occupation gallery at the former Ford Factory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last month, we commemorated Total Defence Day with the Ministry of Communications and Information and the National Archives of Singapore, in conjunction with the opening of the revamped gallery on the Japanese Occupation at the former Ford Factory, where Singapore was surrendered to the Japanese on that day 75 years ago.

sections.label: Guardians of the City card game
sections.summary: A Total Defence strategy card game, Guardians of the City, will be rolled out to all secondary school uniformed groups this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Beyond SAF, we will roll out a Total Defence strategy card game, "Guardians of the City", to all secondary school uniformed groups this year.

sections.label: ACCORD implements 18 proposals
sections.summary: As ACCORD Chairman, the speaker reports that all 18 proposals involving employers, families, communities and educational institutions have been implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As Chairman of ACCORD, I am pleased to update that we have successfully implemented all 18 proposals involving various stakeholders − employers and businesses, families and communities, and educational institutions.

sections.label: Employers and schools on NS
sections.summary: A survey found 96% of employers agreed NS provides needed security, and two schools held NS enlistment sharing sessions for over 700 students and parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In a recent survey, 96% of employers agreed that NS provides the security needed for Singapore to prosper.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, the Global Indian International School and United World College (Southeast Asia), whose principals are ACCORD members, organised sharing sessions to provide more than 700 students and parents with information on the NS enlistment process.

sections.label: Ms Shahane's NSmen workplace measures
sections.summary: Ms Shahane introduced time off for IPPT preparation and half a day extra leave for gold achievers, and received the 2016 NS Advocate Award for Individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Ms Shahane also introduced measures to grant time off work for NSmen employees to prepare for the individual physical proficiency test (IPPT) and reward gold achievers with an additional half day of annual leave, which encourages them to do better in their IPPT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In recognition of her efforts, Ms Shahane was awarded the NS Advocate Award for Individuals in 2016.

sections.label: Civic response and Total Defence
sections.summary: The speaker says the civic-minded response gives confidence in responding to challenges, citing 50 years of NS, a strong SAF and Singaporeans uniting for Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This immediate civic-minded response gives me confidence that we will be able to respond appropriately to any challenges, support one another and recover quickly after any crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have responded with 50 years of NS and a strong SAF, and all Singaporeans coming together for Total Defence.

sections.label: New cyber and fake news division
sections.summary: The speaker found most interesting a new division or group being set up to deal with cyberattacks and fake news, of about 2,600 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The most interesting, from my perspective, was the one on the new division or group being set up to deal with cyberattacks and fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I think it is going to be a big group of about 2,600 people.

sections.label: Cyber defence structure and command
sections.summary: The speaker explains the digital domain's porosity, the tiered structure with CSA under PMO and MCI, and a cyber command protecting MINDEF and SAF amid rising threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The very nature of the digital domain is its porosity and connectivity and you cannot very well just protect one segment because you will be affected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There are different models that MINDEF, SAF and the Government as a whole have studied, and that was the reason why the Cyber Security Agency was set up in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If you look at other countries, some of them are with the prime minister's office, some of them with the Ministry of Defence, but we have chosen to have a tiered structure where CSA is a national defence for cybersecurity under PMO and MCI.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This cyber command is another layer which protects primarily MINDEF and SAF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But because we recognise that our cyber units, our cyber soldiers can be trained and can be deployed as they do for physical key installations in Singapore; that is the concept we are extending.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We are ramping up significantly because the level of the threats has risen and we recognise that the damage can be material.
